hidden_homeroom_d3_low.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_low.text: *At the empty classroom door, the homeroom teacher stops and points down the hall instead of toward the desks inside.* Let's stick to class talk today. Get back to the classroom.

hidden_homeroom_d3_neg.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_neg.text: *She blocks the gap in the door with the attendance book and only points toward the hall.* Personal talk ends here. Go back to your seat.

hidden_nurse_d3_low.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_low.text: *The school nurse stands by the door without pulling out the counseling chair.* It's hard to keep a private session going right now. If you need something, come during official counseling hours.

hidden_nurse_d3_neg.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_neg.text: *She closes the chart binder and doesn't even look toward the chair.* Submit it only through the official desk. Go back to class.

morning3_date_seo_low.name: Seoyeon
morning3_date_seo_low.text: *Seoyeon turns her phone screen on, then right back off. When our eyes meet, she looks down at her clipboard.* I'll post the weekend schedule in the group chat.

morning3_date_dain_low.name: Dain
morning3_date_dain_low.text: *Dain glances this way, then zips her bag all the way up.* This weekend I'm just going to practice on my own.

morning3_date_yuna_low.name: Yuna
morning3_date_yuna_low.text: *Yuna fidgets with the edge of a folded note, then slips it back between the pages.* I'd rather just be alone this weekend.

morning3_start.name: {name}
morning3_start.text: *Friday morning, my third day at the new school. I stayed up watching the blinking message window, turned off my alarm three times and overslept.*

morning3_start_2.name: {name}
morning3_start_2.text: *I clamp the bag strap on my shoulder and run until my breath catches in my throat. A familiar silhouette stands at the gate, right before it closes.*

morning3_seo_gate_1.name: {name}
morning3_seo_gate_1.text: Seoyeon? The bell's about to ring. Why are you still standing here instead of going in? *Seoyeon isn't even shifting her feet in a hurry. She stands beside the gate pillar, looking this way.*

morning3_seo_gate_warm_1.name: Seoyeon
morning3_seo_gate_warm_1.text: *Seoyeon lets out a soft breath and turns the toes of her shoes toward me. Unlike usual, her eyes are those of someone who has been waiting a long while.*

morning3_seo_gate_warm_2.name: Seoyeon
morning3_seo_gate_warm_2.text: I was out for a student council check. I happened to see you running over from way off, too.

morning3_seo_gate_warm_3.name: {name}
morning3_seo_gate_warm_3.text: *A quick glance down: Seoyeon's hands are empty. The approval papers she always carries, and her clipboard, are nowhere in sight.*

morning3_seo_gate_warm_4.name: Seoyeon
morning3_seo_gate_warm_4.text: {name}, catch your breath first. We can walk slowly. We're still fine. *Seoyeon slows her steps to match my breathing. A faint soap scent spreads between our brushing uniform sleeves.*

morning3_seo_gate_2.name: Seoyeon
morning3_seo_gate_2.text: *Seoyeon checks her wristwatch once, then looks up.* You cut it pretty close today.

morning3_seo_gate_3.name: {name}
morning3_seo_gate_3.text: And why are you still at the gate, Seoyeon?

morning3_seo_gate_4.name: Seoyeon
morning3_seo_gate_4.text: So what if we're a little late sometimes. Better we go in together than you stay back and take the demerit alone.

morning3_seo_gate_5.name: {name}
morning3_seo_gate_5.text: The student council president isn't supposed to say that, is she?

morning3_seo_gate_6.name: Seoyeon
morning3_seo_gate_6.text: *The corner of Seoyeon's mouth curves, soft.* I'm joking. I'll explain why we were both late.

morning3_seo_gate_6_b.name: Seoyeon
morning3_seo_gate_6_b.text: *Seoyeon walks up to the teacher on gate duty and opens the student council schedule she brought ahead of time.*

morning3_seo_gate_7.name: Seoyeon
morning3_seo_gate_7.text: It's confirmed. Come on, stay by my side. Let's go in together. *As she folds away the schedule with the confirmation stamp, Seoyeon's shoulder naturally touches my arm.*

morning3_seo_gate_cold_1.name: Seoyeon
morning3_seo_gate_cold_1.text: *Seoyeon brushes past me and turns only a cold glance toward my uniform name tag.*

morning3_seo_gate_cold_2.name: Seoyeon
morning3_seo_gate_cold_2.text: Transfer student. Cutting it close again today.

morning3_seo_gate_cold_3.name: {name}
morning3_seo_gate_cold_3.text: *She doesn't even say my name. Only the neat click of her heels fades quickly.*

morning3_yuna_gate_1.name: {name}
morning3_yuna_gate_1.text: *In the shade beside the gate, Yuna keeps her lashes down and quietly stares at the toes of her shoes.*

morning3_yuna_gate_warm_1.name: {name}
morning3_yuna_gate_warm_1.text: *Yuna had been leaning against the wall. She hears my footsteps and looks up. Her pale fingertips hold out a folded note.*

morning3_yuna_gate_warm_2.name: Yuna
morning3_yuna_gate_warm_2.text: Can I walk to class with you?

morning3_yuna_gate_warm_3.name: Yuna
morning3_yuna_gate_warm_3.text: *The note Yuna hands me, her fingers brushing my palm, has only one line on it.* I waited until you got here.

morning3_yuna_gate_warm_4.name: {name}
morning3_yuna_gate_warm_4.text: I got your note. Thanks for waiting since this morning. *As we walk side by side, Yuna steps half a pace closer and brushes the end of my sleeve.*

morning3_yuna_gate_2.name: {name}
morning3_yuna_gate_2.text: Yuna? Did you oversleep today, too?

morning3_yuna_gate_3.name: Yuna
morning3_yuna_gate_3.text: *Yuna blinks slowly, sleep still in her eyes.* I read all night and didn't notice the sun come up.

morning3_yuna_gate_4.name: {name}
morning3_yuna_gate_4.text: You stayed up the whole night?

morning3_yuna_gate_5.name: Yuna
morning3_yuna_gate_5.text: I wanted to see how it ended. Once I start caring, I can't close it halfway.

morning3_yuna_gate_6.name: Yuna
morning3_yuna_gate_6.text: Have half. This much is enough for me. *Yuna splits the bread she just opened and holds half out. Through the clear bag, the corner of a pale lavender note shows.*

morning3_yuna_gate_6_b.name: {name}
morning3_yuna_gate_6_b.text: *The note tucked under the bag has “You skipped breakfast again” written neatly in pale lavender ink.*

morning3_yuna_gate_7.name: Yuna
morning3_yuna_gate_7.text: Eat slowly while we walk. Don't get crumbs in your bag. Give me the empty wrapper. *Yuna watches the side of my face as I eat the bread she split, takes the empty bag, and folds it small.*

morning3_yuna_gate_cold_1.name: Yuna
morning3_yuna_gate_cold_1.text: *When our eyes meet, Yuna pulls the book in her arms tight up to her chest and goes through the gate first.*

morning3_yuna_gate_cold_2.name: {name}
morning3_yuna_gate_cold_2.text: *Yuna lengthens her stride and slips in among the students ahead. There's not even a gap left to call her name.*

morning3_dain_gate_1.name: {name}
morning3_dain_gate_1.text: *From around the far corner of the gate, Dain sprints at full speed, ponytail flying.*

morning3_dain_gate_warm_1.name: Dain
morning3_dain_gate_warm_1.text: *Dain stops right beside me and pants for breath. Heat comes off her flushed cheeks.*

morning3_dain_gate_warm_2.name: Dain
morning3_dain_gate_warm_2.text: Hey, that was really close! I'm not letting you run alone, so let's go together.

morning3_dain_gate_warm_3.name: Dain
morning3_dain_gate_warm_3.text: {name}, grab my arm. This pace won't leave you out of breath, right? *Dain hooks her elbow through my arm and matches my stride. Where we touch, the warmth spreads clear through the uniform.*

morning3_dain_gate_2.name: Dain
morning3_dain_gate_2.text: Hey, the bell's about to ring! Hurry up and run!

morning3_dain_gate_3.name: Dain
morning3_dain_gate_3.text: Here, grab my hand! It's only fun if we hit the start together. Me going in first alone is boring. *Dain holds out her open palm and lowers her body like she's set on a track.*

morning3_dain_gate_4.name: {name}
morning3_dain_gate_4.text: We'll trip if we hold hands. Let's run side by side.

morning3_dain_gate_4_b.name: Dain
morning3_dain_gate_4_b.text: Fine. Then not even one step behind!

morning3_dain_gate_5.name: {name}
morning3_dain_gate_5.text: *I run shoulder to shoulder with Dain, cutting the wind. The gate that was closing draws up close in front of me.*

morning3_dain_gate_5_b.name: Dain
morning3_dain_gate_5_b.text: Ugh, wait. No, it's nothing. Let's hurry in! *For a second, Dain's right knee gives a little, and her step comes half a beat late.*

morning3_dain_gate_cold_1.name: Dain
morning3_dain_gate_cold_1.text: *Dain slips in with her volleyball teammates and sprints through the gate.*

morning3_dain_gate_cold_2.name: Dain
morning3_dain_gate_cold_2.text: Oh, you're here? Going in first!

morning3_classroom_1.name: {name}
morning3_classroom_1.text: *The moment I open the classroom's back door, the air stiffens from three directions. Seoyeon's fountain pen stops in midair, Dain's chair slides back, and Yuna pushes the bookmark she already set into the same spot one more time.*

morning3_react_seo_1.name: Dain
morning3_react_seo_1.text: Oh? What's this? Coming to school side by side with the student council president, first thing in the morning?

morning3_react_seo_2.name: Yuna
morning3_react_seo_2.text: *Yuna had been looking outside. She catches {name} in the glass, Seoyeon right beside, and silently pushes her bookmark in deep.*

morning3_react_yuna_1.name: Seoyeon
morning3_react_yuna_1.text: *Seoyeon adjusts her grip on the clipboard and looks back and forth between the two of us.* So you walked to school together this morning. You two look pretty close.

morning3_react_yuna_1_b.name: Dain
morning3_react_yuna_1_b.text: *Dain rests an arm on the chair back, turns around, and stares this way.*

morning3_react_yuna_2.name: Dain
morning3_react_yuna_2.text: Wow, I'm jealous. I wish someone waited for me at the gate every morning, too.

morning3_react_yuna_2_b.name: Seoyeon
morning3_react_yuna_2_b.text: *Without a word, Seoyeon walks toward the front door of the classroom and picks up the attendance book.*

morning3_react_dain_1.name: Seoyeon
morning3_react_dain_1.text: You two ran in out of breath first thing this morning. If that took a lot out of you, should I share my lunchbox at lunch?

morning3_react_dain_2.name: Yuna
morning3_react_dain_2.text: *Head down, Yuna draws one short, heavy line in the corner of her notebook.*

morning3_date_intro_b.name: {name}
morning3_date_intro_b.text: *I step into the hall to catch my breath. As if she was waiting, Seoyeon comes up beside me and matches my stride.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_1.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d3_1.text: Teacher, so this is where you were. *I open the door to the empty classroom. The homeroom teacher's fountain pen, running across the desk, falters and stops.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_3.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_3.text: *From the nib she didn't lift in time, one black ink dot spreads on the paper.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_3_b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_3_b.text: *Hiding how flustered she is, the homeroom teacher covers the middle of the page with her palm and quickly turns the manuscript over.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_4.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_4.text: It's nothing. I was just sorting school paperwork. Noticing things quickly is a strength, but right now it's a little awkward.

hidden_homeroom_d3_4_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d3_4_b.text: *Through the back of the flipped page, handwriting revised over and over and red correction marks show through. The homeroom teacher's long, thin fingers press hard on the corner of the manuscript.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_4_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_4_c.text: *She pulls the attendance book over to cover the manuscript, but the edge of the page still sticks out.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_4_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_4_d.text: *Her voice drops half a tone.* What are you staring at. Why come all the way to an empty classroom during break instead of being with your friends.

hidden_homeroom_d3_4_g.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d3_4_g.text: *Red writing in the corner of the first manuscript page: “On hold.” The moment my eyes hit those words, veins rise faintly on the back of the homeroom teacher's hand.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_choice.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d3_choice.text: *Close, with only the desk between us. She cups the edge of the manuscript in her palm and looks at my lips.*
choices: I saw the manuscript paper. Are you writing a novel?
Sorry, I didn't see anything.
Let me be the first to read it when it’s finished.
I’ll read it and point out what needs fixing first.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_1.text: *The tension leaves the homeroom teacher's shoulders, and a low breath slips out.* Too embarrassing to offer as a novel, and I've held on too long to call it a simple exercise. It's already been 7 years.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_1_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_1_c.text: Yeah, 7 years. I wrote the first line back when I was in creative writing in college.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_1_e.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_1_e.text: Around graduation I sent it to the spring literary contest and a few other calls. All rejected. After that, filing a teacher-exam application felt much more realistic than revising the manuscript.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_1_f.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_1_f.text: *She slowly lifts a sheet of the manuscript she had turned over. The handwriting is so fine and dense there's hardly any margin left.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_2.text: The day I waited on my last submission, the acceptance call never came. From that night I put the hope away and started preparing to become a teacher.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_2_b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_2_b.text: I thought I'd forget it once I settled in at school. But every time I moved a drawer, from my rented room to the staff room, this stack always came along.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_2_c.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_2_c.text: You couldn't bring yourself to throw it away, so you brought it all the way here.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_2_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_2_d.text: *She squares the scattered edges of the manuscript, then lets out a small sigh.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_2_e.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_2_e.text: Calling it regret hurts. If I think of it as a stack of paper that's just a waste to throw out, it's a little easier.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_2_f.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_2_f.text: *She runs her fingertips down the worn corner of the manuscript, then leans deep into the chair back.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_3.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_3.text: That's how I became a language arts teacher, teaching other people's writing. Funny, isn't it. I still can't finish even one sentence of my own. I'm just holding the paper.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_3_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_3_b.text: Did you really give it up?

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_3_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_3_c.text: *Her fingers, resting on the manuscript, tremble slightly, then come away a beat late.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4.text: Saying I gave up would be tidy. But if I'm still hiding in an empty classroom every free period, doing this, I guess I haven't finished yet.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4_b.text: *The edge of the manuscript, softened by handling. Her fingertip stays on the last blank line, still unfilled.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4_c.text: *She sets the manuscript stack apart, beside the attendance book.* This is my own work, nothing more. It has nothing to do with class or grading, and it's nothing you need to feel burdened by.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4_d.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4_d.text: Could I read it once, too?

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4_e.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4_e.text: *The homeroom teacher lifts her head and looks me straight in the eye.* I'm thinking of entering it anonymously in the writing club's next open critique. Will you read it properly then?

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4_f.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4_f.text: *She finishes in an even voice, but the tension hasn't left. She slowly rubs the corner of the manuscript with her thumb.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4_g.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_4_g.text: Yes. When it's out on critique day, I'll read it before anyone else.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_choice.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_choice.text: *Morning light falls at a slant over the manuscript paper, where 7 years have settled.*
choices: Seven years isn't giving up — that's persistence
Why do you always write here?
After seven years, isn't it time to let it go?

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_choice_trap.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_choice_trap.text: *Her face goes cold and hard as she closes the manuscript.* I've heard that advice enough over the past 7 years.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_choice_a.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_choice_a.text: *Force goes into her thumb as she smooths the corner of the manuscript. Her eyes soften.* You calling it persistence suddenly makes it feel a lot less pathetic.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_choice_b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_choice_b.text: Once the kids are gone, an empty classroom is much quieter than the staff room. A pretty ironic hideout for a teacher.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_5.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_5.text: Within this week, I'm planning to show it to the other language arts teachers first, too. If I only keep it hidden in a drawer, I don't think I'll ever put the period on it.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6.text: *The homeroom teacher bites her lower lip once, gently, then lets it go, but she does not hide the manuscript in the drawer.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6_b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6_b.text: Until now, every night, I revised it alone and erased it alone. This time I'll actually be judged in front of other people.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6_c.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6_c.text: *The homeroom teacher clears her throat softly and taps the edges of the manuscript into line. In the still classroom, only the wall clock's second hand sounds, clear and sharp.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6_d.text: Thank you. If you hadn't asked first today, I might have gotten scared again and put it at the very bottom of the drawer.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6_e.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6_e.text: *The corner of the manuscript under the homeroom teacher's thumb bends, just slightly.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6_f.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6_f.text: Let's hear the detailed thoughts on the manuscript properly, on the day of the literature club critique.

hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6_g.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_reveal_6_g.text: I should put the rest of the pages in a document envelope. *The homeroom teacher's hand, gathering the manuscript, pauses for a moment over the last blank page.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_hide_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_hide_1.text: All right. For today, let's say we didn't see it. When I'm ready to share it officially, I'll tell the literature club first.

hidden_homeroom_d3_end.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_end.text: *The homeroom teacher puts the manuscript away and opens the window beside the lectern wide. Cool air comes in with the noise from the hall, then soon settles.*

hidden_homeroom_d3_freetalk.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d3_freetalk.text: *The homeroom teacher slips the manuscript neatly into a file folder, leans lightly on the lectern, and looks my way.* You caught a side of me I didn't mean to show. We can talk a little more until the bell.
hidden_homeroom_d3_freetalk.context: Day 3 morning. In an empty classroom, a student found the homeroom teacher's personal novel manuscript. She does not ask the student to keep it secret or give private feedback; she is considering submitting it for an open critique at the literature club.
hidden_homeroom_d3_freetalk.personality: The homeroom teacher once hoped to become a novelist. She never stopped writing after becoming a teacher, but she tries to keep her private creative work separate from her role in teaching and evaluating students.

hidden_nurse_d3_check.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_check.text: *Break is ending, and footsteps grow busy at the far end of the hall.*

hidden_nurse_d3_1.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_1.text: *Next break, I open the nurse's office door with heavy steps. In the smell of antiseptic, the edge of the bandage on my elbow brushes my uniform sleeve.*

hidden_nurse_d3_1_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_1_b.text: *The school nurse looks up from the charts she was sorting, draws her gown closed, and stands.* Oh, back again? Where are you hurt today?

hidden_nurse_d3_1_c.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_1_c.text: I didn't come because I'm hurt.

hidden_nurse_d3_1_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_1_d.text: *She takes half a step toward me and raises an eyebrow a little.* Nothing's hurt. So why the nurse's office?

hidden_nurse_d3_1_e.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_1_e.text: The air in the classroom feels a little suffocating. I'd like to rest a moment, then go.

hidden_nurse_d3_2.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_2.text: You're not running a fever? Your face looks really washed out.

hidden_nurse_d3_3.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_3.text: I just want a quiet moment to catch my breath. It feels like things with people keep getting tangled.

hidden_nurse_d3_3_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_3_b.text: *The school nurse sets the mug she was holding down on the desk without a sound.*

hidden_nurse_d3_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_4.text: *The school nurse draws the curtain by the bed halfway and hands me a paper cup of warm water.* Come sit here. You don't have to hold your face together in here, so take your time and tell me.

hidden_nurse_d3_5_d.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_5_d.text: *As she hands me the cup, the school nurse's warm fingertips brush the back of my hand and lightly press the rim of the paper cup.*

hidden_nurse_d3_5_e.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_5_e.text: Things that are hard to bring up with my classmates keep piling up.

hidden_nurse_d3_5_g.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_5_g.text: I'm afraid of hurting someone, or disappointing them, so I keep putting off the answers I actually need to give.

hidden_nurse_d3_5_h.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_5_h.text: *The school nurse sets her own paper cup neatly on the corner of the desk.*

hidden_nurse_d3_5_i.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_5_i.text: From what I'm hearing, this sounds like a love consultation.

hidden_nurse_d3_5_j.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_5_j.text: Ah, it's not exactly something that big.

hidden_nurse_d3_5_k.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_5_k.text: *She lets out a small laugh.* It's written all over your face. You can't talk your way out of it.

hidden_nurse_d3_5_m.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_5_m.text: I'm not sure this counts as official school-health work, but I'll make an exception and listen, just for today. The bed happens to be empty, too.

hidden_nurse_d3_5_n.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_5_n.text: Have you ever tried to look after everyone around you and found you just couldn't handle it?

hidden_nurse_d3_5_o.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_5_o.text: *The school nurse's eyelashes tremble, and her gaze moves out the window. The rim of the paper cup folds slightly under her thumb.* You asking like that brings the old days back. Where do I even start?

hidden_nurse_d3_5_p.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_5_p.text: There was. Before I came to this school, when I worked on a ward at the university hospital.

hidden_nurse_d3_5_q.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_5_q.text: You worked at a university hospital?

hidden_nurse_d3_choice1.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_choice1.text: *Her profile, hands slipped into the pockets of her gown, is unusually still.*
choices: What happened back then?
You don't have to tell me if it's hard to talk about.
Did you come to the school because you hated the hospital?

hidden_nurse_d3_choice1_a.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_choice1_a.text: I think it's all right to tell you once. It's a story I need to sort out for myself, too.

hidden_nurse_d3_choice1_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_choice1_b.text: Thanks for being considerate. I'll keep it short, only as much as I can handle.

hidden_nurse_d3_choice1_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_choice1_c.text: *She shakes her head, bitter.* I didn't run away just because I hated the work. It wasn't that light a reason, either.

hidden_nurse_d3_6.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_6.text: On the university hospital ward, when the call bells rang from every side at once, I had to weigh every moment which room to run to first. Most days I turned my back before a patient could finish speaking.

hidden_nurse_d3_6_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_6_b.text: *When she sets the water cup down, a round wet mark spreads across the glass.*

hidden_nurse_d3_6_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_6_c.text: I wanted to be a good nurse to everyone, but that ambition wore me down first.

hidden_nurse_d3_6_d.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_6_d.text: Before you moved to the school, did something decisive happen at that hospital? If it's too hard to talk about, you don't have to. *Putting the stethoscope away, she sets her hand on the drawer handle, then quietly draws it back.*

hidden_nurse_d3_6_e.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_6_e.text: There was. One patient I couldn't save in the end. Seventeen, just your age. After I saw that child off, I left the hospital.

hidden_nurse_d3_6_f.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_6_f.text: *The pale green notebook I once saw through a gap in the drawer crosses my mind. Handwriting of a letter that never went on past the first page.*

hidden_nurse_d3_7.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_7.text: That's why I came to this school. Here I'm not chased by call bells, and I can look each student who comes to me in the face, all the way through.

hidden_nurse_d3_8.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_8.text: So say it honestly, starting with the feelings you can actually carry. Don't hold onto everything just to stay a good person to everyone, and suffer alone.

hidden_nurse_d3_8_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_8_d.text: If it's too much to sort out alone, tell me anytime. If you need it, I'll connect you with the counseling center myself.

hidden_nurse_d3_8_e.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_8_e.text: *I fold the counseling card she handed me in half and put it in my uniform pocket.*

hidden_nurse_d3_8_f.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_8_f.text: *I stand and take hold of the nurse's office door handle. When a drawer opens behind me, the corner of the pale green notebook comes to mind again.*

hidden_nurse_d3_8_h.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_8_h.text: Miss, just a moment. *I can't bring myself to open the door, and I turn. The rustle of paper inside the drawer stops.*

hidden_nurse_d3_choice2.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_choice2.text: *The school nurse closes the drawer slowly and looks up at me. In the quiet air that smells of antiseptic, I choose my words.*
choices: Is that why you left the hospital?
Are you okay talking more about it?
Wouldn't you feel better if you told me everything?

hidden_nurse_d3_choice2_a.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_choice2_a.text: Yeah. If I'd forced myself to hold on like that, I thought my hands would shake in front of other patients too.

hidden_nurse_d3_choice2_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_choice2_b.text: Thanks. Today I'll only go as far as I can say without wavering.

hidden_nurse_d3_choice2_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_choice2_c.text: *The school nurse's gaze settles, calm.* Whether it actually eases you is for the person bringing the hurt out to decide. The one listening doesn't get to rush that.

hidden_nurse_d3_9.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_9.text: Coming by when you feel stuck is always welcome. I just can't promise I'll settle all your problems for you.

hidden_nurse_d3_9_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_9_b.text: *I set the empty paper cup down and fidget again with the card I'd put in my pocket.*

hidden_nurse_d3_9_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_9_c.text: If you cross a line you can't handle alone, then I'll help together with your homeroom teacher or the counseling center.

hidden_nurse_d3_9_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_9_d.text: Of course, before that, I'll talk with you first about who we tell, and how much.

hidden_nurse_d3_9_f.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d3_9_f.text: *The sheet lists open times for the nurse's office and the counseling center side by side. I pick up a pen and quietly circle one empty slot.*

hidden_nurse_d3_11.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_11.text: A few minutes are still left before the bell for the next class. If there's more you want to ask, you can say it now.

hidden_nurse_d3_freetalk.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d3_freetalk.text: *The school nurse draws the curtain halfway closed and pulls a chair up close, across from me.* No light jokes today. Let's start with what you really feel.
hidden_nurse_d3_freetalk.context: Day 3. The student came to the infirmary for formal counseling after relationships became complicated, and the school nurse shared her experience of burnout at a university hospital. She keeps her experience separate from the student's burden.
hidden_nurse_d3_freetalk.personality: The school nurse is an experienced medical professional with an easygoing sense of humor. She can discuss her burnout without making the student responsible for her recovery and maintains professional boundaries.

morning3_date_seo_1.name: Seoyeon
morning3_date_seo_1.text: Are you free this weekend? Let's go to the park together.

morning3_date_seo_choice.name: Seoyeon
morning3_date_seo_choice.text: *Seoyeon asks from the classroom doorway. The cap on Dain's water bottle stops turning.*
choices: Sure. What time?
I might be kind of busy.
You’re the student council president. Of course I’ll make time for you.
I’ll clear my schedule if no one else is coming.

morning3_date_seo_accept.name: {name}
morning3_date_seo_accept.text: Yeah, see you this weekend. *I arrange to meet Seoyeon; Dain comes to my desk.*

morning3_date_seo_decline.name: {name}
morning3_date_seo_decline.text: *When I turn down Seoyeon's offer, Dain starts twisting the water-bottle cap again.*

morning3_date_dain_1.name: Dain
morning3_date_dain_1.text: Then it's my turn. Want to hit the arcade this weekend? The president isn't the only one allowed to ask.

morning3_date_dain_2.name: Dain
morning3_date_dain_2.text: I asked out loud. Better than a note, right? *She taps the desk edge.*

morning3_date_dain_choice.name: Dain
morning3_date_dain_choice.text: If you don't hate arcades, you could go with me. Don't just give the president an answer. *She leans down a little, waiting.*
choices: Sure, let's do it
This weekend might be tough.
Since you’re asking that hard, I’ll go.
Make it fun, and you’ve got a deal.

morning3_date_dain_accept.name: {name}
morning3_date_dain_accept.text: Okay. See you at the arcade. *Dain smiles; Seoyeon closes her clipboard.*

morning3_date_dain_decline.name: Dain
morning3_date_dain_decline.text: Oh, yeah? Can't help it if you're busy! It's not because the president asked first, is it?

morning3_date_dain_decline_narr.name: Dain
morning3_date_dain_decline_narr.text: Okay, let's just get ready for the next class! *She smiles, deliberately bright, and goes back to her seat, but just before the bell she taps quickly inside her uniform pocket.*

morning3_date_yuna_1.name: {name}
morning3_date_yuna_1.text: *Just before lunch, Yuna sets a folded note on my desk. Seoyeon and Dain look at her hand at the same time.*

morning3_date_yuna_1_b.name: Seoyeon
morning3_date_yuna_1_b.text: Yuna. If you ask by note, nobody else can hear you.

morning3_date_yuna_2.name: Yuna
morning3_date_yuna_2.text: *The note reads.* Weekend. Used bookstore. Even if you have plans already, come if you want to. — Yuna

morning3_date_yuna_choice.name: Yuna
morning3_date_yuna_choice.text: If saying it aloud matters, I'll say it now. I want your answer. *She looks at Seoyeon, then Dain, leaving her face uncovered.*
choices: Write “I'll go” on the back of the note
Write “I can't this weekend” on the back of the note
Write on the note, “If you don’t want to go alone, I’ll come with you.”
Write on the note, “I’ll go if we keep it secret from everyone else.”

morning3_date_yuna_accept.name: {name}
morning3_date_yuna_accept.text: *I write my answer on the back and return the note. Yuna reads it, folds it and slips it into her book.*

morning3_date_yuna_decline.name: {name}
morning3_date_yuna_decline.text: *I write the refusal on the back of the note and set it on the book. Yuna slips her bookmark in first, and only then looks quietly down at that short sentence.*

morning3_set_multiple.name: {name}
morning3_set_multiple.text: *Dates overlapping on one weekend. I can't bring myself to decide who to ask for understanding first, so I close the calendar on my phone.*

morning3_end.name: {name}
morning3_end.text: *The bell ending the last morning class rings, and lunch comes on like the calm before a storm.*

morning3_gate_none_1.name: {name}
morning3_gate_none_1.text: *Panting, I pass the school gate, but nobody is waiting for me. Overhead, the cold late bell rings.*

morning3_seo_gate_neg_1.name: Seoyeon
morning3_seo_gate_neg_1.text: *Seoyeon doesn't so much as glance at my name tag as she brushes past.*

morning3_seo_gate_neg_2.name: {name}
morning3_seo_gate_neg_2.text: *The steady click of Seoyeon's heels fades quickly inside the gate.*

morning3_yuna_gate_neg_1.name: {name}
morning3_yuna_gate_neg_1.text: *Before our eyes can meet, Yuna turns her head and goes through the gate. No note, either.*

morning3_dain_gate_neg_1.name: Dain
morning3_dain_gate_neg_1.text: *Dain runs into the middle of her sports-club friends and doesn't look this way.*

morning3_dain_gate_neg_2.name: {name}
morning3_dain_gate_neg_2.text: *No greeting, not until the volleyball key chain on the end of Dain's bag turns the corner of the main building.*

morning3_date_seo_neg.name: Seoyeon
morning3_date_seo_neg.text: *She brushes past with the clipboard held to her chest like a shield.* I'll only put the weekend schedule in the class group chat. Don't ask me privately.

morning3_date_dain_neg.name: Dain
morning3_date_dain_neg.text: *She zips her bag all the way up, loud.* Don't call me out this weekend. I'll be practicing alone in the gym.

morning3_date_yuna_neg.name: Yuna
morning3_date_yuna_neg.text: *She starts to take a note from her pocket, then shoves it deep between the pages again.* Don't look for me this weekend.
